blocks.label: Worked Example
blocks.md:
The synthesis of compound **X** takes place in 2 steps:

| OHCCH<sub>2</sub>CHO | $\overset{\mathrm{step}1}{\rightarrow}$ | intermediate | $\overset{\mathrm{step}2}{\rightarrow}$ | HO<sub>2</sub>CCH(OH)CH<sub>2</sub>CH(OH)CO<sub>2</sub>H |
|---|---|---|---|---|
|   |   |   |   | compound **X** |

Which reagents could be used for this synthesis?

**Answer:**

- The first step involves a nucleophilic addition of HCN, with NaCN as catalyst, and heat to form a hydroxynitrile
- In the second step, the nitrile is refluxed with dilute aqueous sulfuric acid causing hydrolysis of the nitrile forming a carboxylic acid and ammonium salt

![Two-step synthesis of compound X from OHCCH2CHO: addition of 2HCN with NaCN catalyst and heat gives a dihydroxy dinitrile; hydrolysis with water and sulfuric acid gives HO2CCH(OH)CH2CH(OH)CO2H and ammonium sulfate.](assets/553e97abfb10-3-9-organic-synthesis-answer-worked-example-two-.png)

blocks.label: Worked Example
blocks.md:
The synthesis of hexanoic acid takes place in 2 steps

| 1-chloropentane | $\overset{\mathrm{reagent}X}{\rightarrow}$ | compound **Z** | $\overset{\mathrm{reagent}Y}{\rightarrow}$ | hexanoic acid |
|---|---|---|---|---|

Which reagents could be used for this synthesis?

**Answer:**

- Halogenoalkanes can undergo **nucleophilic substitution **with ethanolic KCN in which the CN<sup>-</sup> ion acts as a nucleophile and replaces the chlorine atom in 1-chloropentane to form a **nitrile.**
- The treatment of nitriles with dilute hydrochloric acid and heat will produce a carboxylic acid and an ammonium salt.
- In this case, hexanoic acid and ammonium chloride will be formed.

![Step 1: 1-chloropentane reacts with KCN to form compound Z. Step 2: Compound Z reacts with water and HCl to form hexanoic acid and ammonium chloride.](assets/80b53dea3f81-3-9-organic-synthesis-answer-worked-example-synt.png)
